sentiment.rationale: Workday reported strong Q4 results with subscription revenue up 15.7% and non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 30.6%, but forward guidance for FY27 subscription revenue growth of 12-13% is a deceleration from FY26's 14.5% growth, and management explicitly noted a slower pace of margin expansion due to increased AI investment. The guidance was not raised relative to prior expectations (CFO stated 'the guide hasn't changed materially from what we indicated 90 days ago'), and management's tone is optimistic but acknowledges near-term headwinds from the DIA contract and elongated large enterprise deal cycles. The score reflects genuine operational momentum and confident AI narrative, but is tempered by the flat-to-lower forward guidance and explicit investment-driven margin trade-off.

summary.revenue: Q4 total revenues $2.532 billion, up 14.5% YoY; subscription revenues $2.360 billion, up 15.7% YoY. FY26 total revenues $9.552 billion, up 13.1%; subscription revenues $8.833 billion, up 14.5%.
summary.eps: Q4 diluted EPS $0.55 (GAAP), non-GAAP $2.47 (beat expectations of $2.32). FY26 diluted EPS $2.59 (GAAP), non-GAAP $9.23.
summary.guidance: FY27 subscription revenue $9.925-9.950 billion (12-13% growth); Q1 FY27 subscription revenue $2.335 billion (13% growth); FY27 non-GAAP operating margin ~30%; Q1 non-GAAP operating margin 30.5%; FY27 free cash flow $3.180 billion (15% growth).
summary.margin: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin 30.6% (up from 26.4% YoY); FY26 non-GAAP operating margin 29.6% (up from 25.9%). GAAP operating margin Q4 6.9%, FY26 7.5%.
key_risks: Some net new large enterprise deals taking longer to close, particularly in Fed, SLED, healthcare, and parts of commercial market, impacting Q4 net new deal volume.
DIA contract added nearly 1 point to Q4 subscription revenue growth and is not expected to continue in Q1, impacting sequential performance.
Average contract duration down year-over-year due to higher mix of renewal and customer base activity.
Accelerated pace of AI investment across product and go-to-market expected to slow near-term margin expansion.
Restructuring expenses of $303 million in FY26 impacted operating income.
Forward-looking statements subject to risks including security breaches, service outages, competition, privacy regulations, and economic volatility.
key_opportunities: Agentic AI adoption accelerating: Q4 generated over $100 million in new ACV from emerging AI products, growing over 100% YoY; overall ARR from these solutions now over $400 million.
1.7 billion AI actions delivered across platform in FY26; 12 new organically developed role-based agents moving to general availability.
Sana Core and Sana Enterprise released to GA, creating new way for 75 million users to engage with Workday.
Flex Credits consumption-based pricing model gaining traction with nearly 50 customers signed on.
International expansion progress in Canada, EMEA, ASEAN, Japan, and India.
Medium enterprise customers drove roughly 60% of net new ACV in FY26, with Workday GO expansion.

management_tone.label: optimistic
management_tone.justification: CEO Aneel Bhusri stated 'I'm very optimistic about what we're doing on the agentic front' and 'I truly believe that our investments in agentic AI will enable Workday to reaccelerate growth,' while CFO Zane Rowe noted 'we still feel like we've got good momentum' despite acknowledging near-term investment trade-offs.
